body:
Four clicks tell you what your ad is chasing.

Ringg's new AI agents now resolve up to 65% of customer calls (OpenAI, 2026-09-23: https://openai.com/index/ringg). Useful news. But it made me think about a simpler thing most small business owners never check.

Every Meta ad has a setting called Performance goal. It tells Meta what to optimise for: clicks, messages, leads, or something called "conversions" further down your funnel.

Most people never open this screen. They judge the ad by the creative, the image, the caption. Wrong screen entirely.

If your Performance goal is set to "link clicks," Meta will find you people who click. Not people who buy, not people who book, not people who fill your form. Just clickers. Across our own accounts, we track over 7,341 lead-form submissions from nine Meta accounts in India, UK, US and Canada, and that setting is the difference between a form that fills and one that doesn't.

Here's where to look: Ads Manager, your campaign, the ad set, the line that says Performance goal.

Check this before the creative. It decides who Meta goes and finds.

If you want a second pair of eyes on your own account's settings, our audit is free.
